While it could be a stylistic 'cracked meringue' dessert, the geometry of the break looks slightly physically implausible, with thin fragments hanging without clear support or connection to the main body.

The caramel drip has a very smooth, plastic-like viscosity that contrasts sharply with the porous texture of the ice cream. It lacks the subtle surface tension variations usually seen in real viscous liquids.
The wafer cone at the very bottom appears slightly warped and lacks the crisp grid pattern typical of real wafers, appearing somewhat melted or blurred into the hand/background.
